conviction_note: Small net-positive lean. abs_move 8.0 (front straddle 8.63% over 4 days; the baseline's 0.99% event move is an artefact of a 20d realised vol inflated by the mechanical -24% warrant ex-date on 2026-10-14), raised for a first combined-company print with a likely first combined outlook. p_up 54: the positives (synergy-raise precedent, legacy beats, strong TV ad market, insider warrant buy) agree with a very call-heavy skew and a +22% bounce off the low, so they are partly priced; the negatives (leverage credibility, WB studio slump) are widely reported and sit against a crowded short. impact_sum +0.7 and impact_scaled +0.64 agree in sign and size.
bar: Two bars that do not agree. (1) Company guide for the reported quarter (legacy Paramount Skydance only, because the WBD merger closed 2026-10-06, after the 30 Sep quarter end): Q3 revenue $6.95-7.15B, adjusted EBITDA $875-975M, Paramount+ subs flat q/q (Q2 release 2026-08-04, summarised at https://quartr.com/events/paramount-skydance-corporation-psky-q2-2026_3gF238sd; CordCuttersNews gave $6.8-7.0B for revenue). FY26 legacy guide: about $30B revenue, adj. EBITDA $3.8-3.9B. (2) Aggregator consensus that looks pro forma combined: revenue $16.27B, EPS -$0.05 (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/skyd/earnings); a search summary of Benzinga showed $18.36B and TipRanks an EPS of 0.13. So the EPS bar is unsourced/disputed; revenue and EBITDA are sized against the company guide. print_vs_bar_pct is legacy revenue against the $7.05B guide midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest 145.9M shares, 3.5 days to cover on 41.4M ADV, settlement 2026-10-15 (https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/SKYD/short-interest; one source, unverified). Shares outstanding about 5.04B, but the legacy public holders, the only ones who received warrants, held about 471M shares (about 9%; https://finviz.com/news/402595/skydance-provides-details-on-separate-trading-of-skyd-class-b-shares-and-warrants). On that float, SI is roughly 31%: crowded, though warrant delta-hedging (long SKYD.WS, short SKYD) probably inflates it. IBKR borrow about 1.4-2.1% on Oct 7-13 (search summary), so borrow is not tight. Skew is -25.5 vol points (25d calls far richer than puts), put/call OI 0.16, and the baseline reads it as upside paid. Tape: spot 8.285, +2.66% over 5d, -9.55% over 20d (window includes the warrant ex-date), -50.5% from the 52w high, +21.8% off the low, +4.5% intraday on 11-09 per stockanalysis.

findings.finding: The reported quarter is legacy Paramount Skydance only, guided to revenue of $6.95-7.15B and adj. EBITDA of $875-975M (Q3 2025 actual was $952M). The same team beat EBITDA and raised the FY guide to $3.8-3.9B in Q2 (EBITDA +27% to about $1.1B), so EBITDA in the upper half of the guide is likely; revenue has been closer to a miss (Q2 $6.91B vs $7.02B est.).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Predecessor PSKY (same Class B, same management; not in the baseline): on Q2 2026 (Aug 4) an EPS beat plus an FY EBITDA raise brought a conflicting reaction, after-hours slip then about +4.5% next day per Simply Wall St; on Q3 2025 a revenue miss was outweighed by the savings raise (+6.4% after hours).
findings.why_not_priced: This lands inside the company's own guide, so most of it is expected. What is not obviously priced is the beat-and-raise pattern on legacy EBITDA. The market's attention is on the combined balance sheet, and aggregator bars mix in pro forma WBD, so a clean legacy EBITDA beat may be under-modelled. If it were priced, sell-side previews would be talking about legacy EBITDA and they are not.
findings.independence: The Q2 beat and raise: https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/psky-beats-q2-estimates-raises-2026-outlook-as-ceo-stands-firm-on-110-billion-wbd-deal-but-stock-slips-after-hours/cZo5x9qRJ4S (same release, different reporter).

findings.finding: The first post-close call could raise the $6B merger synergy target (70% due within two years). Citi's Bazinet thinks about $8B by 2029 is likely, integration has moved fast since close (eight distribution execs out, five-day-office buyouts, games layoffs, about 2,000 US cuts reported), and at the predecessor's first post-merger call (Nov 2025) management raised its savings target from $2B to $3B+.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-11-10 Q3 2025 release raised the savings target by $1B to at least $3B, gave a $30B revenue guide and added a $1.5B investment plan; PSKY rose about 6.4% after hours even though revenue missed (https://newsable.asianetnews.com/markets/paramount-skydance-stock-pops-as-ceo-unveils-3b-savings-drive-bigger-film-slate-retail-lauds-best-earnings-call-in-2-years-articleshow-mm8fmq3).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades about 30% below the $12 at which $47B of equity was raised, at about $42B market cap, and Debtwire models only $1.75B of synergies realised in 2027. A credible raise is not in that price. If it were priced, the stock would sit nearer the $12 deal price or the $10 Citi and Huber targets. This is an inference from a precedent and one analyst, not a company document.
findings.independence: Debtwire base-case synergy path and the $6.0bn target: https://ionanalytics.com/insights/debtwire/skydance-corporation-synergies-alone-wont-hit-leverage-targets-credit-report/ (2026-10-14). Integration and layoff pace: https://www.adweek.com/dealroom/layoffs-on-the-way-as-skydance-now-controls-paramount-and-wbd/

findings.finding: Leverage credibility is the overhang. Net debt is $78.9B per the company (Debtwire says $84.3B). Leverage is 4.3x on a synergised basis by management's count, 6.16x on realised synergies (Debtwire) and 7.8x (Fitch). S&P expects negative FCF in 2026-27, the new debt carries 6.30-8.90% coupons, and Debtwire's base case misses the 2028 (<3.75x) and 2029 (3x) targets. The first combined call has to defend a path that credit analysts say needs asset sales or equity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Only the debt news itself is on record: PSKY dipped on the $44.4B debt package launch (2026-09-28, https://parameter.io/paramount-skydance-psky-stock-dips-as-company-unveils-massive-44-4b-debt-package-for-wbd-acquisition/), and the WSJ of 2026-10-30 reported the market doubts the balance-sheet figures (stockanalysis headline list). No print has yet carried a combined FCF or leverage outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is 50% off its high and the debt worry is in every article. The part that is not priced is the first company-level FCF and leverage bridge, which could disappoint (negative FCF guided) or relieve (asset sales). Sized small and against a crowded short and a call-heavy skew. Financing question answered: the debt bought the WBD acquisition, not distress. The risk is the speed of deleveraging, not solvency (liquidity is about $10B).

findings.finding: Warner Bros.' film slate collapsed in 2026: Supergirl opened at $38M and faces a $100M+ loss, Practical Magic 2 lost money, and WB's box-office share fell from 21% in 2025 to 6%. Studios weakness at WB enters any combined Q4 or 2027 outlook the company gives, though not the legacy Q3 reported here.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No combined-company print exists. WBD's own studio swings moved WBD (e.g. Q3 2025 theatrical +74%), but WBD no longer reports (Form 15 filed 2026-10-16).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since it is widely reported. What could still surprise is the size of film write-downs or impairments in a combined Q4 guide. Net of the rest of the company: studios are a minority of EBITDA (linear is about two-thirds per TheWrap), and HBO Max and Paramount+ are the growth lines, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Studio-wide share data: https://www.comicbasics.com/warner-bros-just-hit-a-box-office-milestone-it-hasnt-seen-in-25-years-and-not-the-good-kind/ (secondary). WBD reporting suspended: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001437107

findings.finding: The TV ad market was strong in the September quarter and into December. Fox's quarter ended 2026-09-30 showed total ad revenue +47% and TV ad revenue +60% (World Cup plus higher political, midterm year), and management said ad demand remained strong heading into its December quarter. That is a counterparty read for CBS political and local ads in Q3 and especially Q4, against Paramount's Q2 linear ad decline of -14%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Linear advertising was the line PSKY's Q2 2026 release flagged as the weak spot (-14%), and the stock moved only a few percent. No clean reaction on an ad beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This came after Paramount last spoke (Aug 4 guide), so the Q3 guide predates it. Much of Fox's lift is World Cup, which CBS did not carry, and the political figure is not quantified, so the transmission to CBS is uncertain. Proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy only; no Skydance or CBS-specific ad data found. TheWrap on the Fox quarter: https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/fox-corporation-earnings-q1-2027/

findings.finding: The bar mismatch: aggregators carry Q3 revenue of $16.27B and EPS of -$0.05 (pro forma combined, with WBD), while the reported quarter is legacy Paramount at about $7B per the company guide. That invites 'revenue miss' headlines in the first minutes after the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this structure. The predecessor's Q3 2025 release also printed below the revenue consensus and still rose on guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Automated headline traders key off aggregator consensus. By the close of the next session the mismatch should be understood, so most of the effect fades inside the window. Sized small and mostly after-hours.
findings.independence: Company Q3 guide (legacy only): https://quartr.com/events/paramount-skydance-corporation-psky-q2-2026_3gF238sd. Merger closing date 2026-10-06: https://virginiabusiness.com/paramount-skydance-completes-warner-bros-merger/

findings.finding: Positioning: about 145.9M shares short (settlement 2026-10-15), roughly 31% of the about 471M legacy public float (Class B public holders) though likely inflated by warrant hedging, against a -25.5 vol-point call skew and put/call OI of 0.16. Shorts are crowded and option buyers are long upside going into the first combined print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Following the 2026-10-14 warrant ex-date crash (-22 to -24%), the stock bounced +21.8% off its low, including an almost 11% day with no news (per search summary of an asktraders item).
findings.why_not_priced: The skew already prices upside, so a squeeze is partly paid for. The other side is that call-heavy retail positioning after a +22% bounce sets up a sell-the-news risk, hence a small positive with a wide band.
findings.independence: Float denominator (471M warrant-eligible public shares): https://finviz.com/news/402595/skydance-provides-details-on-separate-trading-of-skyd-class-b-shares-and-warrants. Skew from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Director Gerald Cardinale (RedBird Capital) bought 4.9M SKYD warrants ($12 strike, 2036 expiry) at $2.80 on 2026-10-16, about $13.7M, two days after the warrant ex-date crash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy reaction on record for this entity.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 2026-10-20 and small against a $42B cap, but it is a long-dated levered insider bet on the stock above $12. Note that the CFO's 2026-10-15 Form 4 was only RSU vesting with tax withholding at $7.26, not a buy. If insiders' conviction were widely read, the warrant would trade richer. Small.
findings.independence: CFO Form 4 (vesting only, not a buy): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2041610/000122520826008446/doc4.xml

findings.finding: Sell-side turned more constructive into the print. Huber Research upgraded to Overweight with a $10 target (2026-10-28, with another Huber upgrade listed on 11-06), Citi resumed at Buy with $10 (10-27) and JPMorgan resumed at Neutral with $9, against an average target of about $9.15 and a Hold consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell on the Citi resumption day (10-27) per the stockanalysis headline list.
findings.why_not_priced: Already in the price via the run-up off the low; filed for completeness.

findings.finding: The $0.05 quarterly dividend (about $1.07B a year on the about 5B-share count per Debtwire's model) sits awkwardly beside S&P's negative-FCF view for 2026-27 and the leverage targets. The first combined call could cut or suspend it to fund deleveraging.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No dividend change since the 2025 Skydance merger; the rate has held at $0.05.
findings.why_not_priced: No one has flagged a cut. It is an inference, and a cut to accelerate deleveraging could be read neutral or even positive by a credit-focused market. The yield is about 2.4%. Small.
findings.independence: Dividend history: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/paramount-skydance-corporation-declares-quarterly-cash-dividend-to-class-a-and-class-b-shareholders-ce7e50d3da8bf326. Shares the Debtwire document with the leverage finding.

findings.finding: On the day of the print, the stockanalysis headline list carries a THR/TheFly report that James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as DC Studios co-CEOs, with Latcham named DC chief (Variety/Reuters). Mainstream October reporting had them staying. A creative-leadership reset at DC follows the Supergirl loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. The stock was +4.5% intraday on the same day.
findings.why_not_priced: Same-day news; immaterial to a $42B company's earnings. Unverified beyond an aggregator headline list.

outside_window.finding: Warrant dilution: 470.75M warrants at $12 (full cash exercise about $5.65B) are out of the money at $8.29 and matter only if the stock rallies above $12; the company's early-expiry call needs $30 for 20 of 30 days after 2029-10-13.
Management leverage targets (<3.75x in 2028, 3.0x in 2029) and the >$10B FCF by 2030 target are tested only years out.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean agrees with the strongly call-paid skew (-25.5) and the +22% bounce off the low, so it is probably partly priced. The negatives (leverage, WB studio) cut against a crowded short and that skew, which is why they are sized small.
lessons_applied: Rule 1/6: the reported-quarter finding lands inside the company guide and the predecessor's reaction to the last beat-and-raise was mixed, so 0.6 -> 0.4.
Rule 5: the synergy-raise finding is an inference from a precedent and one analyst, not a company document, so 1.2 -> 1.0; the Fox ad-market read is a proxy, 0.4 -> 0.3.

Rule 7: the negatives sit against a -25.5 call skew and about 31% SI on the legacy float, so leverage -1.0 -> -0.7 and WB studio -0.6 -> -0.4; Rule 9 (segment, net of the rest) also applied to the studio finding.
Rule 4: the debt financing was asked what it buys (the WBD acquisition, liquidity about $10B); signed as a deleveraging-pace concern, not distress.
Rule 6: the EPS bar is disputed (pro forma aggregator vs legacy guide); revenue and EBITDA sized against the company guide, and the mismatch finding kept small.
Net: the sum is unchanged at +0.7 (the cuts offset); p_up 55 -> 54, expected_move 0.8 -> 0.64.
